source.original_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space and let (X,Y) have joint probability law P, with X standard Gaussian and Y square integrable. For any real polynomial p and any probability rho on the unit sphere S, define the predictor and actual data potential by the integrals below. The potential V_rho is smooth on all of E. For every real radius R and derivative order n, there is a finite nonnegative constant C, chosen before rho and w, that bounds the norm of D^n V_rho(w) for every sphere probability rho and every ambient w with norm at most R.

E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel sigma algebra. No positive dimension is assumed; an empty sphere has no probability law to instantiate.
P is a probability on E times R whose first marginal is exactly the standard Gaussian on E. The label Y is in L2(P); no independence or higher label moment is assumed.
p is any real polynomial. No parity, coefficient normalization, prescribed degree cutoff or conditional teacher relation is assumed.
For each R and n, the bound C may depend on P, p, E, R and n, but is uniform over rho and w. Order zero is included; a negative radius gives an empty spatial condition.

\begin{gathered}V_\rho\in C^\infty(E;\mathbb R)\quad(\rho\in\mathcal P(S)),\\\forall R\in\mathbb R\ \forall n\in\mathbb N\ \exists C\ge0:\\\forall\rho\in\mathcal P(S)\ \forall w\in E,\\\|w\|\le R\ \Longrightarrow\ \|D^nV_\rho(w)\|\le C.\end{gathered}

Ambient spatial regularity of the literal statistical potential only. Drift and covariance regularity, time measurability, weak-equation uniqueness, process construction, law symmetry, centering and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities require separate arguments.

lean.statement:
anonymous_statement : ∀
  {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [inst_2 : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [inst_3 : MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] (P : MeasureTheory.Measure (E × ℝ))
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P],
  MeasureTheory.Measure.map Prod.fst P = ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E →
    ∀ (p : Polynomial ℝ),
      MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun z => z.2) 2 P →
        let S := { w // ‖w‖ = 1 };
        have V := fun ρ w =>
          2 *
            ∫ (z : E × ℝ),
              (∫ (v : S), Polynomial.eval (Inner.inner ℝ (↑v) z.1) p ∂ρ - z.2) *
                Polynomial.eval (Inner.inner ℝ w z.1) p ∂P;
        (∀ (ρ : MeasureTheory.Measure S), MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ρ → ContDiff ℝ (↑⊤) (V ρ)) ∧
          ∀ (R : ℝ) (n : ℕ),
            ∃ C,
              0 ≤ C ∧
                ∀ (ρ : MeasureTheory.Measure S),
                  MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ρ → ∀ (w : E), ‖w‖ ≤ R → ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n (V ρ) w‖ ≤ C
decoder_context: All typeclasses and operators in the printed statement are standard Mathlib objects. The real inner product is literal Inner.inner R; the subtype S carries its induced Borel sigma algebra. stdGaussian E is the standard Gaussian probability on the finite-dimensional real inner-product space E. MemLp f 2 P means square integrability. The integral notation denotes the Bochner integral with Mathlib total semantics, returning zero when integrability fails; notation alone must not be read as a new integrability hypothesis or assertion.

The displayed smoothness order ContDiff R (up-arrow top) uses the coercion of the top of ENat into the extended smoothness-order type ENatOmega. It denotes C-infinity, not the analytic top order omega. iteratedFDeriv R n is the total n-fold Frechet derivative as a continuous multilinear map; at order zero its norm equals the norm of the function value. Its norm for positive orders is the multilinear operator norm. The definition of V and every dependence on the sphere measure are printed literally.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianPolynomialRidgeSmooth
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianPolynomialFeatureGradient
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Bounds

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped ENNReal InnerProductSpace ContDiff

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianPolynomialPotentialSmooth

open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianPolynomialRidgeSmooth
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianPolynomialFeatureGradient

/-- The actual data potential is ambient smooth, with local derivatives uniformly bounded
over every probability measure on the unit sphere. Only an L2 label is required. -/
theorem gaussian_polynomial_joint_potential_smooth_uniform_derivatives
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (P : Measure (E × ℝ)) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (hGaussian : P.map Prod.fst = stdGaussian E)
    (p : Polynomial ℝ) (hlabel : MemLp (fun z : E × ℝ => z.2) 2 P) :
    let S := {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1}
    let V : Measure S → E → ℝ := fun ρ w =>
      2 * ∫ z : E × ℝ,
        ((∫ v : S, p.eval ⟪(v : E), z.1⟫_ℝ ∂ρ) - z.2) *
          p.eval ⟪w, z.1⟫_ℝ ∂P
    (∀ ρ : Measure S, IsProbabilityMeasure ρ → ContDiff ℝ (∞ : ℕ∞ω) (V ρ)) ∧
    ∀ (R : ℝ) (n : ℕ), ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧
      ∀ ρ : Measure S, IsProbabilityMeasure ρ →
        ∀ w : E, ‖w‖ ≤ R → ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n (V ρ) w‖ ≤ C := by
  classical
  intro S V
  let : CompleteSpace E := FiniteDimensional.complete ℝ E
  obtain ⟨hf, hdf, D, M₁, M₂, _, _, _, _, _, _, hRep⟩ :=
    gaussian_polynomial_joint_feature_gradient_representation P hGaussian p hlabel
  let F : E → Lp ℝ 2 P := fun w =>
    (hf w).toLp (fun z : E × ℝ => p.eval ⟪w, z.1⟫_ℝ)
  let label : Lp ℝ 2 P := hlabel.toLp (fun z : E × ℝ => z.2)
  let mean : Measure S → Lp ℝ 2 P := fun ρ => ∫ v : S, F v.1 ∂ρ
  obtain ⟨hg, hgSmooth⟩ := standard_gaussian_polynomial_ridge_L2_smooth (E := E) p
  have hmarg : MeasurePreserving (Prod.fst : E × ℝ → E) P (stdGaussian E) :=
    ⟨measurable_fst, hGaussian⟩
  let J : Lp ℝ 2 (stdGaussian E) →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 P :=
    Lp.compMeasurePreservingₗᵢ ℝ Prod.fst hmarg
  have hF : ContDiff ℝ (∞ : ℕ∞ω) F := by
    have he : F = fun w => J ((hg w).toLp (fun x : E => p.eval ⟪w, x⟫_ℝ)) := by
      rfl
    rw [he]
    exact J.toContinuousLinearMap.contDiff.comp hgSmooth
  have hV (ρ : Measure S) (hρ : IsProbabilityMeasure ρ) :
      V ρ = fun w : E => 2 * ⟪mean ρ - label, F w⟫_ℝ :=
    (hRep ρ hρ).2.2.2.1
  let L (ρ : Measure S) : Lp ℝ 2 P →L[ℝ] ℝ :=
    (2 : ℝ) • innerSL ℝ (mean ρ - label)
  have hVL (ρ : Measure S) (hρ : IsProbabilityMeasure ρ) : V ρ = L ρ ∘ F := by
    rw [hV ρ hρ]
    rfl
  refine ⟨fun ρ hρ => ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [hVL ρ hρ]
    exact (L ρ).contDiff.comp hF
  · obtain ⟨B, hB⟩ := (isCompact_closedBall (0 : E) 1).exists_bound_of_continuousOn
      hF.continuous.continuousOn
    have hB0 : 0 ≤ B := (norm_nonneg (F 0)).trans (hB 0 (by simp))
    have hMean (ρ : Measure S) (hρ : IsProbabilityMeasure ρ) : ‖mean ρ‖ ≤ B := by
      let := hρ
      have hbound : ∀ᵐ v : S ∂ρ, ‖F v.1‖ ≤ B :=
        Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun v => hB v.1 (by simpa using v.property.le)
      simpa only [mean, Measure.real, measure_univ, ENNReal.toReal_one, mul_one] using
        norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const hbound
    have hL (ρ : Measure S) (hρ : IsProbabilityMeasure ρ) :
        ‖L ρ‖ ≤ 2 * (B + ‖label‖) := by
      have hr : ‖mean ρ - label‖ ≤ B + ‖label‖ :=
        (norm_sub_le _ _).trans (add_le_add (hMean ρ hρ) le_rfl)
      simpa only [L, norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2),
        innerSL_apply_norm] using mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hr (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2)
    intro R n
    have hn : (n : ℕ∞ω) ≤ (∞ : ℕ∞ω) :=
      WithTop.coe_le_coe.mpr (le_top : (n : ℕ∞) ≤ ⊤)
    obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := (isCompact_closedBall (0 : E) R).exists_bound_of_continuousOn
      (hF.continuous_iteratedFDeriv hn).continuousOn
    refine ⟨2 * (B + ‖label‖) * max C 0, by positivity, ?_⟩
    intro ρ hρ w hw
    rw [hVL ρ hρ]
    exact ((L ρ).norm_iteratedFDeriv_comp_left hF.contDiffAt hn).trans
      (mul_le_mul (hL ρ hρ) ((hC w (by simpa using hw)).trans (le_max_left _ _))
        (norm_nonneg _) (by positivity))

#print axioms gaussian_polynomial_joint_potential_smooth_uniform_derivatives

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.GaussianPolynomialPotentialSmooth

notation.text: S is the unit sphere; f_rho is the sphere-averaged polynomial predictor.
The actual joint-data integral potential, evaluated at any ambient point w.

The iterated Frechet derivative and its multilinear operator norm. Smoothness is proved, so the total Lean operators are classical derivatives here. At order zero the norm is the absolute value of the potential.
H is joint-data L2; F is the polynomial feature class, ell is the label class, and m_rho is the Bochner mean of the feature.

steps.title: Pull the smooth Gaussian feature into joint-data L2
steps.text: The existing polynomial ridge theorem gives a smooth map into Gaussian L2. Pullback by the first coordinate is a linear isometry into H, because the input marginal is exactly Gaussian. Its image is the actual polynomial feature class F. The membership witnesses are proof-irrelevant; no response differentiation or extra response moment is used.
steps.lean:
classical
  intro S V
  let : CompleteSpace E := FiniteDimensional.complete ℝ E
  obtain ⟨hf, hdf, D, M₁, M₂, _, _, _, _, _, _, hRep⟩ :=
    gaussian_polynomial_joint_feature_gradient_representation P hGaussian p hlabel
  let F : E → Lp ℝ 2 P := fun w =>
    (hf w).toLp (fun z : E × ℝ => p.eval ⟪w, z.1⟫_ℝ)
  let label : Lp ℝ 2 P := hlabel.toLp (fun z : E × ℝ => z.2)
  let mean : Measure S → Lp ℝ 2 P := fun ρ => ∫ v : S, F v.1 ∂ρ
  obtain ⟨hg, hgSmooth⟩ := standard_gaussian_polynomial_ridge_L2_smooth (E := E) p
  have hmarg : MeasurePreserving (Prod.fst : E × ℝ → E) P (stdGaussian E) :=
    ⟨measurable_fst, hGaussian⟩
  let J : Lp ℝ 2 (stdGaussian E) →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 P :=
    Lp.compMeasurePreservingₗᵢ ℝ Prod.fst hmarg
  have hF : ContDiff ℝ (∞ : ℕ∞ω) F := by
    have he : F = fun w => J ((hg w).toLp (fun x : E => p.eval ⟪w, x⟫_ℝ)) := by
      rfl
    rw [he]
    exact J.toContinuousLinearMap.contDiff.comp hgSmooth

steps.title: Identify the literal data potential
steps.text: The existing joint-feature representation supplies the integrability and the displayed identity for the actual double integral. For each law, pairing with its residual is a continuous linear functional. Composition with the smooth feature therefore proves ambient smoothness.
steps.lean:
have hV (ρ : Measure S) (hρ : IsProbabilityMeasure ρ) :
      V ρ = fun w : E => 2 * ⟪mean ρ - label, F w⟫_ℝ :=
    (hRep ρ hρ).2.2.2.1
  let L (ρ : Measure S) : Lp ℝ 2 P →L[ℝ] ℝ :=
    (2 : ℝ) • innerSL ℝ (mean ρ - label)
  have hVL (ρ : Measure S) (hρ : IsProbabilityMeasure ρ) : V ρ = L ρ ∘ F := by
    rw [hV ρ hρ]
    rfl
  refine ⟨fun ρ hρ => ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [hVL ρ hρ]
    exact (L ρ).contDiff.comp hF

steps.title: Bound every residual uniformly over the parameter law
steps.text: Continuity of F on the compact unit ball gives a nonnegative bound B. Integrating its norm against a probability law bounds every feature mean by B. The label has one fixed finite L2 norm, so every residual and every pairing functional have the same bound.
steps.lean:
· obtain ⟨B, hB⟩ := (isCompact_closedBall (0 : E) 1).exists_bound_of_continuousOn
      hF.continuous.continuousOn
    have hB0 : 0 ≤ B := (norm_nonneg (F 0)).trans (hB 0 (by simp))
    have hMean (ρ : Measure S) (hρ : IsProbabilityMeasure ρ) : ‖mean ρ‖ ≤ B := by
      let := hρ
      have hbound : ∀ᵐ v : S ∂ρ, ‖F v.1‖ ≤ B :=
        Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun v => hB v.1 (by simpa using v.property.le)
      simpa only [mean, Measure.real, measure_univ, ENNReal.toReal_one, mul_one] using
        norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const hbound
    have hL (ρ : Measure S) (hρ : IsProbabilityMeasure ρ) :
        ‖L ρ‖ ≤ 2 * (B + ‖label‖) := by
      have hr : ‖mean ρ - label‖ ≤ B + ‖label‖ :=
        (norm_sub_le _ _).trans (add_le_add (hMean ρ hρ) le_rfl)
      simpa only [L, norm_smul, Real.norm_of_nonneg (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2),
        innerSL_apply_norm] using mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hr (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2)

steps.title: Transfer compact bounds on every derivative
steps.text: For each R and n, continuity of the n-th feature derivative gives a finite nonnegative bound M on the compact closed ball. Continuous-linear composition multiplies this bound by the common residual-functional bound. The resulting C is independent of the parameter law and evaluation point. The same rule includes order zero.
steps.lean:
intro R n
    have hn : (n : ℕ∞ω) ≤ (∞ : ℕ∞ω) :=
      WithTop.coe_le_coe.mpr (le_top : (n : ℕ∞) ≤ ⊤)
    obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := (isCompact_closedBall (0 : E) R).exists_bound_of_continuousOn
      (hF.continuous_iteratedFDeriv hn).continuousOn
    refine ⟨2 * (B + ‖label‖) * max C 0, by positivity, ?_⟩
    intro ρ hρ w hw
    rw [hVL ρ hρ]
    exact ((L ρ).norm_iteratedFDeriv_comp_left hF.contDiffAt hn).trans
      (mul_le_mul (hL ρ hρ) ((hC w (by simpa using hw)).trans (le_max_left _ _))
        (norm_nonneg _) (by positivity))
